full_sentence: Rarely, if ever, has a novelist managed such vivid characterisation.
acceptable_variants: seldom has a novelist managed such vivid characterisation.

options.text: a novelist has managed such vivid characterisation.
options.why_wrong: After a negative adverbial such as 'rarely, if ever', the auxiliary must come before the subject; leaving the normal word order is ungrammatical.

options.text: a novelist manages such vivid characterisation.
options.why_wrong: The present simple gives a plain statement and loses both the inversion and the negative emphasis that the stem sets up.

options.text: has a novelist managed such vivid characterisation.
did a novelist manage such vivid characterisation.
options.why_wrong: 'Did' places the event in a simple past with no link to the present, but the adverbial 'rarely, if ever' requires present perfect inversion.

grammar_focus: Subject-auxiliary inversion after the negative adverbial 'rarely, if ever'
explanation: A negative adverbial placed at the start of a sentence requires inversion of the auxiliary verb and subject, so the present perfect 'has ... managed' must come before 'a novelist'.
